title: PACKET — a specialist return
description: The envelope+narrative return contract from ADR-0015. Authored source for the prose is docs/process/communication-registers.md; where this schema and that document disagree, the process doc wins. DELIBERATELY FLAT WITH NO $ref — do not factor out shared subschemas. Two independent reasons, and both must fail before the constraint is worth relaxing: (1) a flat schema converts cleanly to a GBNF-style grammar for grammar-constrained decoding in a future harness port, and $ref indirection does not; (2) flatness is what makes the hand-rolled zero-dependency Node validator about 40 lines instead of a dependency. NOT EXPRESSIBLE HERE: finding_count must equal claims.length. JSON Schema cannot relate two sibling values, so that assertion belongs to the validator (ADR-0015 Slice 3), not to this file. Everything else in the correspondence rule — no fact only in narrative, no claim only in claims[] — is prose discipline and must never be described as enforced.

v.description: Schema version. Required. A contract that ships to strangers without a version key has no migration signal at its first breaking change and no way for a consumer to tell which contract it holds. Four bytes, and the only affordance that makes v2 survivable.

agent.description: Which persona is returning, as the .claude/agents/<name>.md stem. Deliberately a pattern rather than an enum of the roster: personas.md and the agent files are already checked against each other by scripts/check-canon.mjs, and a third copy of the roster here would be a third thing to drift.

state.description: Did this invocation finish, or stop early? An agent that ran out of turns says so here. A return that says nothing at all is the false green the whole contract exists to prevent, so this key is required and has no default.

finding_count.description: How many findings. MUST equal claims.length — asserted by the validator, not here. Two sources for one number is a defect in a v1 schema; the assertion makes them one, and it makes a smuggled finding unreportable rather than merely unrecorded, because an agent that wants a finding to count has to put it in claims[] where it is counted.

claims.description: The findings themselves. Never capped: capping the record is dropping findings, and finding thirteen would simply go unreported.

epistemic.description: How the claim was established, using the same three grades as the Done Gate's proof ladder, because it is the same ladder — the gate grades an item, a claim grades itself. One vocabulary, two subjects. These three are the whole set; nothing else is valid under v: 1. Grade honestly in both directions: forcing a taste call to look deterministic is as wrong as eyeballing something a one-line check would settle.

severity.description: Matches the vocabulary the review lenses already use (.claude/agents/code-reviewer.md). One set of words for one concept: a finding's severity in a packet means what it means in a review document.

evidence.description: What the claim rests on. Required as a key; may be empty only when the grade allows it. For deterministic, this must name what was RUN — a grade is a claim about what was actually executed, so it decays silently when the command behind it goes missing.

then.description: A deterministic claim with empty evidence is malformed. That pairing is the entire reason the tag exists: "the agent said it looked clean" and "this command exited 0, here it is" are different epistemic states that plain prose renders identically. FOR SLICE 3'S VALIDATOR: hardcode this single conditional rather than implementing a generic draft-07 if/then engine, treat an `if` failure as skip-then rather than as an error, and INTERSECT this `then` with the base schema rather than replacing it — otherwise `evidence` loses its type check on exactly the claims that most need one, and it fails open. The validator must throw on any keyword it does not implement: one that silently no-ops produces a pass certifying nothing, which is the laundered false green this contract exists to stop.

unknowns.description: What the agent could not determine. MANDATORY, and may be empty. An empty array is an assertion — "I looked, and there was nothing I couldn't determine" — while a missing key is a defect. Those are different claims and the schema must not let them collapse into each other, which is why this key has no default and is listed in required.

narrative.description: The persona's own voice, written as that agent would write it. The coordinator gates on the envelope and FORWARDS this — it does not paraphrase it into house style, because a coordinator that rewrites every specialist into one voice has paid for the persona and thrown away what it bought. The narrative must CARRY each finding, not flavour it: every claim reappears with its path, its severity, and its action. "This one's ugly. Fix it before it ships." is a failing narrative. Where voice and precision pull against each other, clarity beats character.

x-register-legend.description: Voice intensity is edge-conditioned, and a schema that treated all prose alike would not carry that. The test is WHO CONSUMES THE TEXT, not who carries it — transport is not consumption.
x-register-legend.damped: Machine-consumed prose: parsimony and pragmatism, no set-pieces, no extended metaphors, no jokes. Identity survives in word choice and in what the agent puts first, not in performance.
x-register-legend.full-voice: The persona as written, unhedged. Its receiver is the human even though its wire is internal — the coordinator only relays it.
